title: Your Phone Bill Just Got Weird (And Nobody's Talking About It)
excerpt: RAM prices are skyrocketing, AI is eating CPU like crazy, and it's about to hit your business harder than you think.

content.text: So here's something that caught my eye today — and honestly, it should catch yours too. Memory prices just hit levels we haven't seen since 2007. Like, twenty years of steady price drops? Basically gone. In a matter of months.

Why? AI. Everyone's racing to build AI infrastructure, and it's creating this insane demand for RAM and computing power. The big cloud providers are gobbling up capacity, pushing prices up everywhere else, and smaller businesses are getting squeezed in the middle.
What This Actually Means for You
You might be thinking, "Intecha, I don't buy RAM. This doesn't affect me." But actually? It does. Here's how:

items: If you use cloud services — VoIP platforms, CRM systems, email hosting, anything hosted on AWS or Azure — your provider's infrastructure costs just went up. Some of that trickles down to you.
If you've been thinking about upgrading your server or computer systems, the timing just got worse. Hardware refresh cycles are getting more expensive.
If you're considering AI tools for your business (answering services, chatbots, call analytics), the underlying cost to run those tools is climbing. Pricing might follow.

content.text: Memory prices are at 2007 levels. The last two decades of technology getting cheaper? That's reversing — at least for now.

This isn't some random market blip. It's a sign that AI infrastructure demand is completely outpacing supply. Big tech companies are literally telling their engineers to stop wasting CPU cycles because capacity is so tight. That's real pressure, and it's reshaping how computing infrastructure gets priced and allocated.

content.label: Intecha's Take
content.text: Don't panic, but do pay attention. If you've got upcoming tech purchases or system upgrades on your roadmap, get quotes now before this gets worse. And if a vendor suddenly raises prices on your hosted services, ask them directly if infrastructure costs are the reason. Most of them will be honest about it — this is too widespread to hide. Also? Be skeptical of "AI-powered" solutions that suddenly seem way more expensive than before. Sometimes it's real value. Sometimes it's just passing along higher infrastructure costs.
